source.description: Project APDU load point where OpenSC requests and receives attacker-controlled COOLKEY object-list bytes into object_info.
source.note: The libFuzzer harness only supplies a fake reader. The scored source is the OpenSC card parser load path: coolkey_list_object passes object_info as the receive buffer to coolkey_apdu_io/sc_transmit_apdu; the fake reader fills that APDU response from the PoC.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled APDU response bytes are loaded into the COOLKEY object_info structure.; value `object_info`; from `return coolkey_apdu_io(card, COOLKEY_CLASS, COOLKEY_INS_LIST_OBJECTS, seq, 0,`

sink.description: ASan crash location: coolkey cleanup frees o->data for each object-list entry, and the malformed object list made two entries share the same allocation.

root_cause.description: Root cause: attacker-controlled object_id is accepted into a new list entry without checking that the ID is unique. Duplicate IDs later cause coolkey_fill_object to attach one allocated data buffer to two object records, which is freed twice during cleanup.

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant parsed value: the object ID parsed from attacker-controlled object_info.
tainted_value_origin.note: The PoC supplies duplicate object_id values through object_info; object_len at the next line is parsed from the same APDU response.

coarse_trace.summary: Loads attacker-controlled COOLKEY object-list APDU response bytes into object_info through coolkey_apdu_io/sc_transmit_apdu.
Parses object_id and object_len from object_info and iterates over card-reported objects.
Creates a new object-list entry from attacker-controlled object_id without rejecting duplicate IDs.
Later PKCS#15 emulation performs template lookup and requests attributes for an object with the duplicated ID.
Reads object data and assigns the same allocated data pointer to both the located duplicate entry and the caller object.
Card disconnect invokes COOLKEY cleanup after the PKCS#15 read path finishes.
Iterates all object-list entries and frees o->data, hitting a second free of the shared pointer.

fine_trace.note: OpenSC asks the card/fuzz reader for the next object-list APDU response and stores it in object_info. This is the project parser/load point, not LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput.
Materializes the attacker-controlled object ID from the APDU response. The PoC repeats this ID across object records.
Parses the object length from the same attacker-controlled response; this length controls later object allocation size.
Propagates the parsed object metadata into the object-list builder for each listed object.

The vulnerable code copies the attacker-controlled ID into a new list entry without first checking whether that ID already exists. The developer patch adds the missing uniqueness check in this function before object data/list insertion.
The duplicate-ID object is inserted into the list, preserving two logical entries that can later resolve to the same object ID.
ASan allocation context. The object data buffer for the duplicate-ID object is allocated using attacker-derived object length.
Lookup by duplicated obj->id can return a different list entry from the caller object, because duplicate IDs were admitted earlier.
Stores the allocation into the found list entry.
Stores the same allocation into the caller object. When obj and obj_entry are different entries with the same ID, two list records now share one data pointer.
Card disconnect dispatches cleanup for the COOLKEY private object list.
ASan reports double-free here. The cleanup loop frees o->data for each object-list entry; because duplicate entries share the same pointer, the second visit frees an already-freed allocation.
